title: Terrain heightmap source asset (M25)
description:
TEACHING NOTE — Terrain heightmap schema.
This schema describes a height-sample grid used to author terrain patches for the vertical slice project.
The baker (tools/creation_engine.py bake-terrain) converts this JSON into a compact TRN1 binary that the C++ TerrainRenderer loads with LoadCooked().

Design:
  • A terrain patch is a W×H grid of floating-point height samples.
  • The world position of sample [row][col] is:
      x = col * cellSize + originX
      y = heights[row * width + col]  (the stored value, in metres)
      z = row * cellSize + originZ
  • Adjacent patches are tiled by offsetting origin by (width-1)*cellSize.
  • Minimum valid grid: width=2, height=2 (one quad, two triangles).
  • Physics integration: the C++ BakeTerrainCollider() function accepts width/height
    that are powers of 2 (Jolt HeightFieldShape requirement).  Authors should prefer
    power-of-2 dimensions (4, 8, 16, 32, 64) for terrains that will have physics.

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI — points to this schema file.

version.description: SemVer string for the terrain asset format.  Breaking changes bump major version.

name.description: Human-readable name of the terrain patch shown in the editor.

description.description: Optional editorial notes about this terrain patch.

width.description: Number of height samples along the X axis.  Must be >= 2. For physics integration, prefer powers of 2 (4, 8, 16, 32, …).

height.description: Number of height samples along the Z axis.  Must be >= 2. For physics integration, prefer powers of 2.

cellSize.description: World-space distance (in metres) between adjacent height samples. A 16×16 grid with cellSize=4.0 covers a 60×60 m patch (15 cells × 4 m per cell).

items.description: Height value in metres (Y coordinate in world space).  Negative values are allowed for underwater terrain.

heights.description: Row-major flat array of height samples. Length must equal width × height. Row 0 corresponds to Z=0 (south edge); the last row is the north edge.
